predecessors.name: Kingdom of Georgia
predecessors.text: Kakheti, the rump George VIII kept after he 'was captured in 1465' and 'ruled Kakheti as an anti-king until his death in 1476'

successors.name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti
successors.text: Kakheti united with Kartli as the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti under Erekle II, 'after Teimuraz II's death' on 8 January 1762; Cliopatria draws this union as its 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (55,276 km2 in…

ledger.x: 1466: Kakheti becomes a kingdom under George VIII.
1513: Kartli conquers Kakheti for a time.
1648: Persia ousts Teimuraz I and sets Rostom over Kakheti.

c. 1664: the capital moves from Gremi to Telavi. Infobox: 'Gremi (1466-1664)'; Archil 'made [Telavi] his capital in place of Gremi which was ruined by the Iranian invasions'. The infobox gives 1664 as Gremi's last year; the page gives no year for the move.
1703: the House of Kakheti is restored.
1744: Nader ends the occupation and makes Erekle II king of Kakheti.
8 January 1762: Kakheti and Kartli unite under Erekle II.
1762: the Kingdom of Kakheti ends in the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1578-1590)
wars.outcome: By the treaty of 21 March 1590 the Safavids ceded 'Azerbaijan, Karabagh, Ganja, Dagestan and Qarajadagh, as well as parts of Georgia'.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618)
wars.outcome: Abbas I's armies captured Tbilisi and 'both Kartli and Kakheti became Safavid dependencies once again' (1603-1604 section); the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha of 20 November 1612 'secured the 1555 borders envisaged by the Peace of Amasya'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages; Kakheti's northern (Tusheti, Pshavi), eastern (Shirvan, Dagestan) and Hereti limits are approximate and the pages give none.
